title: Analysis of the interplay between hepatitis B virus-positive hepatocytes and Kupffer cells ex vivo using mice as a model
protocol: Select 8-week-old C57BL/6 mice weighing about 19–25 g.
Mix 20 μg HBV DNA with a volume of DPBS equivalent to 8% of the mouse body weight.
Warm mice with a heat lamp for 3-5 minutes before injection to dilate tail blood vessels.
Be cautious not to overheat the mice.
Dilute ketamine 10-fold with DPBS.
Anesthetize the mouse by intraperitoneal injection of 20 μL of diluted ketamine.
Immobolize the mouse with a restrainer.
Locate the dilated vein on the ventral side of the tail, near the tip.
Wipe the intended injection site with an alcohol pad for disinfection.
Add 8% body weight-equivalent DNA-saline solution to the syringe.
Connect the needle to the syringe.
Tap the syringe to move air bubbles to the needle.
Expel air from the syringe until a small amount of solution is visible.
Insert the needle in the distal portion of the mouse tail nearly parallel to the tail.
Inject the entire volume of the DNA solution into the tail vein within 5–8 seconds.
Remove the mouse from the restrainer and place it into the cage for recovery.
Anesthetize the mouse for blood collection.
Grasp the mouse with the thumb and index finger using the non-dominant hand.
Find the hairless freckles on the side of the jaw.
Prick a freckle with a lancet near the base of the ear or mouth.
Prick the freckle of the mouse with a lancet.
Collect 100–500 μL of blood in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Return the mouse to its cage.
Centrifuge the collected blood sample at 12,000 × g for 5 minutes between 18°C and 25°C.
Transfer the supernatant (serum) into a new Eppendorf tube.
Store the serum at -20°C or -80°C as needed.
Measure HBV surface antigen (HBsAg) levels in the mouse serum using an ELISA kit according to the manufacturer’s protocols.
Measure e antigen (HBeAg) levels in the mouse serum using an ELISA kit according to the manufacturer’s protocols.
Pre-warm Solution A and Solution B in a 42°C water bath.
Prepare 70% ethanol solution (in spray and in a bottle).
Autoclave at least 50 mL of water.
Perfuse the mouse liver twice: first with a solution containing EGTA and BSA, then with a solution containing collagenase.
Use Percoll to isolate hepatocytes.
Use OptiPrep density gradient to separate Kupffer cells from other nonparenchymal cells.
Pre-clean the pump with 70% ethanol for more than 5 minutes.
Flush the pump system with at least 50 mL of autoclaved water and ensure all water is removed.
Fill the pump system with Solution A.
Circulate Solution A (38°C–39°C) through the pump using a rate of 7 ml/min.
Anesthetize the mouse with ketamine as described in step 7.
Apply 70% ethanol to the mouse abdomen for disinfection.
Place the sedated mouse on the operation board and fix the mouse legs to the board with tape.
Open the abdominal cavity.
Cut open the mouse abdomen to access internal organs.
Move the intestine to the right to uncover the venous systems.
Insert a suture under the upper part of the portal vein and hold both ends with a hemostat.
Place another suture under the upper part of the vena cava beside the right kidney and tie a loose knot.
Open the thoracic cavity by cutting the diaphragm and chest bones beside the xiphisternum.
Grab the xiphisternum with a tweezer and open the chest over the mouse face to unveil the heart.
Puncture the heart’s center using the sharp end of a 24-gauge catheter.
Insert the 24-gauge catheter into the right auricle, allowing it to reach the inferior vena cava downstream of the liver.
Start perfusing the liver with Solution A at a flow rate of 7 mL/min.
Cut the portal vein with a scissor after lifting suture 1.
Lift suture 2 by grabbing both suture ends to remove remaining blood in the liver and then tie suture 2.
Perfuse the liver with a total volume of 50 mL of Solution A.
Monitor the flowing of Solution A through the liver.
Transfer the liquid inflow tube of the perfusion pump to the tube containing pre-warmed Solution B after perfusion of 50 mL Solution A.
Be careful not to trap any air bubble during transfer.
Perfuse the liver with at least 25 mL but no more than 40 mL of Solution B at a flow rate of 7 mL/min.
Continue the perfusion until the liver is swollen and shiny.
Stop the pump and cut the inferior vena cava in the upper region of suture 2.
Quickly remove the liver from the mouse abdominal cavity.
Place the liver in a petri dish with 35 mL of Solution C.
Hold the liver with tweezers and gently tap the perfused liver to disperse cells from the liver.
Continue the process until all liver lobes disintegrate and separate into single cells.
Filter liver cells with a 70 μm nylon cell strainer.
Centrifuge the cells in a 50 mL tube at 60 × g for 2 min, both acceleration and break set at 3 to separate NPCs (supernatant) and hepatocytes (pellet).
Prepare the Percoll solution by mixing 5.2 mL of 10× Percoll buffer with the Percoll stock solution to a final volume of 40 mL.
Keep the Percoll solution at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant, which contains NPCs, to a new tube on ice for later purification of Kupffer cells.
Leave behind a little bit more than 3 mL of the solution and the pellet, which contained hepatocytes, in the tube.
Add 30 mL of diluted Percoll solution to the pelleted cells in the tube.
Gently resuspend the cells by pipetting.
Avoid vortexing.
Centrifuge at 1,200 × g in Eppendorf 5804R centrifuge for 3 min at 18°C–25°C.
Cells pelleted are purified hepatocytes.
Count cells and seed them (at a density of 0.3 × 106/mL) in hepatocyte culture medium in a collagen-coated plate.
Centrifuge the supernatant isolated in step 33b at 583 × g for 8 minutes at 18-25°C.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 5.5 mL DMEM.
Overlay cells on a step gradient consisting of OptiPrep Density Gradient Media with densities of (from top to bottom) 1.035, 1.042, 1.056, and 1.081.
Centrifuge at 21,400 × g for 20 minutes at 18-25°C using a Beckman SW40Ti rotor.
Isolate Kupffer cells at the interface of densities 1.042 and 1.056.
Mix isolated Kupffer cells with 5 mL DMEM in a 15 mL tube.
Pellet cells at 583 × g for 8 minutes at 18-25°C.
Resuspend Kupffer cells in 5 mL DMEM.
Pellet cells at 583 × g.
Resuspend cells in 5 mL DMEM.
Repeat pelleting and resuspending steps once more to rinse Kupffer cells.
Remove the supernatant carefully, leaving behind 1-2 mL medium depending on pellet size.
Stain dead cells with trypan blue.
Count purified Kupffer cells using a hemocytometer.
Plate Kupffer cells in Kupffer cell culture medium.
Incubate plates in a 5% CO2 incubator at 37°C for 3 hours.
Remove nonadherent cells with an aspirator.
Resuspend Kupffer cells by treatment with trypsin at 37°C for 3 minutes if necessary.
Verify the purity of Kupffer cells by flow cytometry.
Rinse cells once with DPBS.
Incubate cells in hepatocytes culture medium.
Change the medium every three days for long-term culturing.
Place Transwell inserts gently in each well above freshly attached hepatocytes using sterile forceps.
Plate Kupffer cells at a density of 2 × 10^6 cells per Transwell insert.
Co-culture Kupffer cells and HBV-positive hepatocytes in a medium containing a 1:1 ratio of hepatocytes culture medium and Kupffer cells culture medium for three days.
Collect the conditioned medium on day 1 after co-culturing.
Replace the conditioned medium with fresh medium on day 1.
Collect the conditioned medium again on day 3.
Measure the levels of HBsAg using a commercial ELISA kit following the manufacturer’s protocol.
Measure the levels of HBeAg using a commercial ELISA kit following the manufacturer’s protocol.
Prepare the Seahorse analyzer and microplate for the OCR assay 30 minutes before starting.
Prepare the assay medium for the OCR assay 10 minutes before starting.
Prepare compound stock solutions and working solutions for the OCR assay 15 minutes before starting.
Load compound solutions into the ports of the Seahorse analyzer 25 minutes before running the assay.
Run the OCR assay for approximately 4 hours.
Analyze the data from the OCR assay for 30 minutes.
Turn on the Agilent Seahorse XFe/XF Analyzer.
Allow the analyzer to warm up for at least 5 hours.
Seed 105 Kupffer cells per well in Seahorse XF plate.
Use appropriate medium for the cell culture.
Add water to the Seahorse XF sensor box.
Place calibrators in a non-CO2 incubator for 16 hours at 37°C.
Prepare XF medium and XF supplement in the cell culture hood.
Transfer sufficient amount of XF medium to a 50 mL tube.
Prepare the assay medium by supplementing Seahorse XF DMEM with 1 mM pyruvate, 2 mM glutamine, and 10 mM glucose.
Warm up the assay medium in a 37°C water bath before use.
Take the foil bag and decapper out from the Seahorse XF Cell Mito Stress Test Kit box.
Open the bag and remove the three test tubes containing oligomycin (blue cap), FCCP (yellow cap), and rotenone/antimycin A (red cap).
Place the removed test tubes on a small test tube rack.
Insert the decapper’s tines into the cap’s inner lip and remove the cap from each tube.
Resuspend the contents of each tube with the volumes of assay medium shown in the Solution 1 table.
Gently pipet the medium up and down about 10 times to dissolve the compound.
Use the compound stock solution to prepare the working solution for loading into the injection port on the sensor cartridge.
Mix 600 μL stock solution of oligomycin (100 μM) with 2,400 μL DMEM in the polystyrene reservoir.
Load 20 μL diluted oligomycin (20 μM) per port using a multichannel pipette.
Prepare 2–3 mL of working solution for each compound in the analytical medium, using the volumes shown in the Solution 2 table for the XFe/XF96 analyzer.
Load compound solutions into the ports on sensor cartridge.
Remove the Seahorse XF cell culture microplate from the 37°C CO2 incubator and examine it under a microscope to confirm cell confluency.
Rinse Kupffer cells twice with 200 μL of Seahorse XF DMEM assay medium, leaving 20 μL behind after each rinse.
Add 160 μL of Seahorse XF DMEM assay medium to each well to achieve a final volume of 180 μL/well.
Place the Seahorse XF cell culture microplate at 37°C without CO2 for 45 min to 1 h before running the assay.
Open the Wave software and retrieve the saved assay template file.
Browse and open the saved design file in the Wave software.
Select the Review and Run tab and click Start Run.
Place the sensor box with the calibration plate into the instrument.
Click “I am ready” when prompted to start calibration.
Wait until calibration is complete (approximately 15–30 minutes).
Ensure that the microplate orientation is correct and remove the cartridge lid if necessary.
Load the Seahorse XF cell culture microplate after equilibration.
Click “I am ready” to initiate the assay.
Turn on the Seahorse XFe/XF96 Analyzer and let the temperature stabilize.
Seed 105 Kupffer cells per well in the Agilent Seahorse XF Cell Culture Microplate using the Kupffer cells culture medium.
Hydrate a sensor cartridge in Seahorse XF Calibrant medium in a non-CO2 incubator at 37°C for 16 hours.
Select the Template for XF Glycolytic Rate Assay in Wave on the XFe/XF96 analyzer.
Make necessary group modifications to tailor the template for the specific assay design.
Prepare Agilent Seahorse Glycolytic Rate assay medium: mix XF DMEM with 1 mM pyruvate, 2 mM glutamine, and 10 mM glucose.
Transfer a sufficient amount of XF medium to a 50 mL tube.
Warm up the assay medium in a 37°C water bath.
Remove the Seahorse XF cell culture microplate from the 37°C CO2 incubators.
Examine the plate under a microscope to confirm confluency and good cell morphology.
Rinse cells twice with 200 μL warm Seahorse XF DMEM assay medium using a multichannel pipette.
Leave 20 μL behind after each rinse.
Incubate cells in 160 μL of Seahorse XF DMEM assay medium per well for 45–60 min at 37°C in a non-CO2 incubator.
Remove the assay medium and add 160 μL of fresh and warm Seahorse XF DMEM assay medium to each well, achieving a final volume of 180 μL/well.
Prepare stock compounds by removing the foil bag from the kit box and opening it.
Take out the red cap vial Rot/AA and the green cap vial 2-DG.
Tap the vials to ensure that the powder is at the bottom before opening them.
Prepare the relevant assay medium as shown in the Solution 3 table using a P1000 pipette.
Vortex the tubes for 1 min to thoroughly dissolve the compounds.
Load the compound into Port A for injection of Rot/AA in the hydrated sensor cartridge.
Load the compound into Port B for injection of 2-DG in the hydrated sensor cartridge.
Download the Agilent Seahorse Glycolytic Rate template into the Seahorse XFe analyzer.
Select Seahorse XF Glycolytic Rate Assay template from the list of available templates and click Design.
Confirm or modify the default groups and conditions in specific assays in the section Groups/Conditions.
Place the sensor box with the calibration plate into the instrument and click “I am ready” when prompted.
Remove the cartridge lid and double-check to ensure that the microplate orientation is correct.
Calibrate and equilibrate the cell culture microplate.
Click “I am ready” when prompted to start.
Load the Seahorse XF cell culture microplate.
Click “I am ready” to run the assay.
